The flowchart illustrates the 'MATRIX MULTIPLY UTILITY (MM)'. It begins with a 'START' block labeled 'U,MM00'. The first step is to 'SAVE RETURN LINKAGES AND INPUT ARGUMENTS'. This is followed by a loop starting with 'MM100 (U,V001) FORM VECTOR DOT'. Inside the loop, the first element is stored, followed by another 'MM100 (U,V001) FORM VECTOR DOT', then the second element is stored, followed by a third 'MM100 (U,V001) FORM VECTOR DOT', and finally the third element is stored. A decision point 'MATRIX MULTIPLICATION COMPLETE' follows. If the answer is 'NO', the process moves to 'MM200 SET TO FORM ELEMENTS FOR NEXT ROW' and then loops back to the first 'MM100 (U,V001) FORM VECTOR DOT' step. If the answer is 'YES', the process proceeds to 'EXIT RETURN'. The 'R2' register is indicated as being used in the 'MM100' steps.

2.36 ORBITAL GUIDANCE MANEUVER PROCESSOR (MP)

Function

The function of the Maneuver Processor is to initialize the parameters for proper execution of the orbital guidance maneuvers. This module is executed only one time for each maneuver.

Entries

M.MP00 Entry made via variable HOP constant from the orbital guidance module.

M.MP50 Entry made from Timer 2 when it is time for a new maneuver.

M.MP55 Entry made from Timer 2 when it is time for a generalized maneuver.

External

E.QT Next Maneuver Processor Entry (M.MP50)

E.Q Maneuver Processor (M.MP50)

E.Q Maneuver Processor (M.MP55)

U.SC00 Sine-Cosine Utility

D.VACTReal Time Clock reading associated with D.VTAS or D.VTNM*
D.VTBTime elapsed in current time base*
D.KT5Time base 5 start time from GRR*

V.SPMInertial pitch angle in pirads or sine of pitch delta from
local horizontal		*
*

horizontal		*
*
V.CPMCosine of pitch delta from local horizontal
V.CYWCosine of yaw delta from local horizontal
F.SCAHFlag to indicate S/C returned control
F.SLRSpecial local reference maneuver first pass flag

G.MPCKVariable HOP to either the Maneuver Processor or next Orbital
Guidance instruction

None.

2.37 MINOR LOOP SUPPORT (MS)

Function

The Minor Loop Support module calculates the attitude increments (delta chi's) used by the Minor Loop module and calculates the terms of the platform to body coordinate transformation used by the Minor Loop module.

Entries

M.MS00 Entered from the Non-Interrupt Sequencer once per computation cycle during Phase 1. Entered from the Phase II Control module once per second during Phase 2.

External

U.SC00 Sine-Cosine Utility
U.TR00 Real Time Telemetry Delay Utility *
E.ENBL Enable interrupts
E.IHBT Inhibit interrupts

Input Data

D.VLM1 Maximum permitted rate of change of roll command chi per Minor Loop
D.VLM2 Maximum permitted rate of change of the yaw and pitch command chi's per Minor Loop
D.VGCX Guidance Chi X (Desired roll gimbal angle) *
D.VGCY Guidance Chi Y (Desired pitch gimbal angle) *
D.VGCZ Guidance Chi Z (Desired yaw gimbal angle) *
D.VCCX Commanded Chi X (Rate limited roll gimbal angle) *
D.VCCY Commanded Chi Y (Rate limited pitch gimbal angle) *
D.VCCZ Commanded Chi Z (Rate limited yaw gimbal angle) *
D.VMLR The number of minor loops per computation cycle

D.VTHX Total roll gimbal angle *
D.VTHY Total pitch gimbal angle *
D.VTHZ Total yaw gimbal angle *
D.VIMR Reciprocal of the number of minor loops per pass through Minor Loop Support
D.FDC0 Bypass setting delta chi's flag

Output Data

D.VDCX Delta Chi X (Roll commanded chi increment) *
D.VDCY Delta Chi Y (Pitch commanded chi increment) *
D.VDCZ Delta Chi Z (Yaw commanded chi increment) *
D.VA1
D.VA2
D.VA3
D.VA4
D.VA5		 } Coefficients used to convert the inertial platform readings to body frame attitude corrections
D.FSMC Steering Misalignment Correction inhibit flag *
D.VGCZ Guidance Chi Z (Desired yaw gimbal angle) *
D.FDC0 Bypass setting delta chi's flag

Status Words

None.

Telemetry

Item PIO Tag Description
D.VDCX 1451 Delta Chi X (Roll commanded chi increment) *
D.VDCY 1455 Delta Chi Y (Pitch commanded chi increment) *
D.VDCZ 1445 Delta Chi Z (Yaw commanded chi increment) *
V.THZT 0015 Yaw gimbal angle at time of delta chi computations *
V.THXT 0021 Roll gimbal angle at time of delta chi computations *
V.THYT 0025 Pitch gimbal angle at time of delta chi computations *
V.CCZT0501Command Chi Z at time of delta chi computations
V.CCXT0505Command Chi X at time of delta chi computations
V.CCYT0511Command Chi Y at time of delta chi computations
V.DCHI2024Delta Chi RTC reference

Initial Conditions

D.VMLR must be initialized to number of minor loops executed per computation cycle. D.VLMR must be initialized to reciprocal of number of minor loops executed per computation cycle. D.VLM1 and D.VLM2, rate change limits, are to be initialized to mission specifications.

Notes

The quantities D.VMLR and D.VLMR must be altered by the program whenever the rate of the minor loop is altered or the computation cycle length is changed considerably.

The guidance chi Z will be magnitude limited to 45 degrees.

    MS100 --> MS200
    MS200 --> MS210
    MS210 --> MS250
    MS250 -- YES --> MS300
    MS250 -- N3 --> MS300
    MS300 --> MS320
    MS320 --> MS400
    MS400 --> MS430
    MS430 --> MS450

The flowchart, titled "MINOR LOOP SUPPORT (MS)", outlines a sequence of processing steps. It begins at MS100, which involves commanding the yaw gimbal. This is followed by MS200, where delta chi values are computed. The process then moves to MS210 to read the roll gimbal angle from the telemetry. At MS250, a decision is made regarding the limit of delta chi. If the limit is exceeded (N3), the flow proceeds to MS300; otherwise (YES), it also proceeds to MS300. MS300 involves inhibiting delta chi and computing SMC compensation. The flow then continues to MS320 to read the pitch gimbal angle, followed by MS400 to compute sine and cosine coefficients, MS430 to handle minor loop support items, and finally MS450 to exit and return.

The flowchart, titled "MINOR LOOP SUPPORT (MS)", begins at a "START MSS70" block. It proceeds to a decision diamond: "IS DELTA CHI VALUE NEGATIVE". If "YES", it goes to an "EXIT RETURN" block. If "NO", it moves to another decision diamond: "IS DELTA CHI VALUE GREATER THAN THE LIMIT". If "YES" here, it goes to a process block "MS510 SET DELTA CHI = + LIMIT", then to a process block "SET SMC FLAG FOR LIMITED CHI", and finally to an "EXIT RETURN" block. If "NO" here, it goes directly to an "EXIT RETURN" block. From the "NO" path of the second decision, it moves to a third decision diamond: "IS DELTA CHI GREATER THAN THE LIMIT". If "YES" here, it goes to a process block "MS520 SET DELTA CHI = - LIMIT", then to a process block "SET SMC FLAG FOR LIMITED CHI", and finally to an "EXIT RETURN" block. If "NO" here, it goes directly to an "EXIT RETURN" block. The "NO" path from the third decision also leads to the "EXIT RETURN" block.

2.38 MATRIX TRANSPOSE UTILITY (MT)

Function

The function of the Matrix Transpose Utility module is to form and store the transpose of a specified matrix.

Entries

U.MT00 Entered by any Non-Interrupt Sequencer and Periodic Processor module.

External

None.

Input Data

See Notes.

Output Data

See Notes.

Status Words

None.

Telemetry

None.

Initial Conditions

None.

Notes

Upon entry, a computer word of the form STO B; CLA A must be in the accumulator, where A is the initial location of the matrix to be transposed and B is the initial location of the matrix in which the transpose is to be stored.

Both matrices are to be grouped in vector form using the VEC assembler pseudo-operation. The three vectors required to represent a 3x3 matrix must be stored using the MAT assembler pseudo-operation.

The matrices A and B may be the same. In that case, the A matrix is transposed and the transpose is then stored over A. Matrices may be grouped by either column or row vectors.

Upon exit, the transposed matrix will be stored in the matrix specified by the word on entry.

MATRIX TRANSPOSE UTILITY (MT)

U.MT00

graph TD; A[START U.MT00] --> B[SAVE RETURN LINKAGE AND INPUT ARGUMENTS]; B --> C[FORM TRANSPOSE MATRIX]; C --> D[EXIT RETURN];

The flowchart consists of four rectangular boxes with dotted borders, arranged vertically. The first box contains the text "START U.MT00". A vertical dotted line with a downward-pointing arrow connects it to the second box, which contains "SAVE RETURN LINKAGE AND INPUT ARGUMENTS". Another vertical dotted line with a downward-pointing arrow connects the second box to the third box, which contains "FORM TRANSPOSE MATRIX". A final vertical dotted line with a downward-pointing arrow connects the third box to the fourth box, which contains "EXIT RETURN".

2.39 BOOST NAVIGATION (NE)

Function

The function of the Boost Navigation module is to determine the vehicle position and velocity in an earth centered inertial coordinate frame.

Entries

M.NE00 Entered from the Non-Interrupt Sequencer once per computation cycle during Phase 1.

External

M.GR00 Gravitation Acceleration
U.SR00 Square Root Utility
U.FD00 Fixed Point Divide Utility
U.TR00 Real Time Telemetry Delay Utility

Input Data

D.VDT Elapsed time between current and previous computation cycle
accelerometer reads in seconds *

D.VZDM Z component of measured velocity (m/sec)
D.VOZM Previous Z component of measured velocity
D.VXDM X component of measured velocity (m/sec)
D.VOXM Previous X component of measured velocity
D.VYDM Y component of measured velocity (m/sec)
D.VOYM Previous Y component of measured velocity
D.VGX X component of gravity acceleration
D.VGY Y component of gravity acceleration
D.VGZ Z component of gravity acceleration
D.VT3I Second phase IGM time-to-go *

F.HSPF High Speed Loop flag
V.GDVB Thrust decay velocity bias

Output Data

D.VXSX component of radius vector, in S-system*
D.VYSY component of radius vector, in S-system*
D.VZSZ component of radius vector, in S-system*
D.VXDSX component of velocity vector, in S-system*
D.VYDSY component of velocity vector, in S-system*
D.VZDSZ component of velocity vector, in S-system*
D.VOXMPrevious X component of measured velocity
D.VOYMPrevious Y component of measured velocity
D.VOZMPrevious Z component of measured velocity
D.VVSTotal space-fixed velocity
D.VV0Second previous total velocity*
D.VV1Previous total velocity*
D.VV2Current total velocity*
D.VIT1Length of second previous computation cycle*
D.VIT2Length of previous computation cycle*
V.GTVBTime bias for thrust decay for high cutoff accuracy

Status Words

None.

Telemetry

ItemPIO TagDescription
D.VZS0034Z component of radius vector, in S-system*
D.VGX0064X component of gravity acceleration
D.VXS0044X component of radius vector in S-system*
D.VGY0070Y component of gravity acceleration
D.VYS0050Y component of radius vector, in S-system*
D.VGZ0060Z component of gravity acceleration
D.VIOR0054Inverse of radius*
D.VXDS 0114 X component of velocity vector, in S-system *
D.VYDS 0120 Y component of velocity vector, in S-system *
D.VZDS 0110 Z component of velocity vector, in S-system *
D.VVS 0124 Total space-fixed velocity
V.IGZ 1074 Z component of gravity velocity
V.IGX 1100 X component of gravity velocity
V.IGY 1104 Y component of gravity velocity

Initial Conditions

Previous components of measured velocity (D.VOZM, D.VOXM, and D.VOYM) must be set to zero at start of mission as well as the components of gravity velocity (V.IGX, V.IGY, and V.IGZ).

The components of earth rate (V.XDO, V.YDO, and V.ZDO) must be computed at mission start.

Previous components of gravity acceleration (V.OGX, V.OGY, V.OGZ) must be set to initial gravity values at start of mission. Previous components of position (V.OXS, V.OYS, and V.OZS) must be computed at start of mission as well as total velocity (D.VVS).

Notes

At a fixed time prior to S-IVB cutoff, a second iteration is made to the square root algorithm to obtain a more accurate total space-fixed velocity. Also at this time, velocity and time values are stored for second order extrapolation in the S-IVB Cutoff Prediction module.

2.40 NAVIGATION EXTRAPOLATION (NI)

Function

This module will compute the extrapolated positions between the navigation computations made by the Orbit Navigation module.

Entries

M.NI00 Entered by the Phase II Control module once per second except on the eight second boundaries when the Orbit Navigation module is executed.

External

U.TR00 Real Time Telemetry Delay Utility

Input Data

D.VNTMTime in mission from GRR of navigation extrapolation*
D.VXDSX component of velocity vector, in S-system*
D.VYDSY component of velocity vector, in S-system*
D.VZDSZ component of velocity vector, in S-system*
D.VXSX component of radius vector, in S-system*
D.VYSY component of radius vector, in S-system*
D.VZSZ component of radius vector, in S-system*
V.NTMOTime of previous navigation pass

Output Data

D.VXSX component of radius vector, in S-system*
D.VYSY component of radius vector, in S-system*
D.VZSZ component of radius vector, in S-system*
V.NTMOTime of previous navigation pass

Status Words

None.

Telemetry

ItemPIO TagDescription
V.XS0144X component of radius vector, in S-system*
V.YS0150Y component of radius vector, in S-system*
V.ZS0134Z component of radius vector, in S-system*

Initial Conditions

None.

Notes

None.

2.41 NAVIGATION UPDATE IMPLEMENTATION (NU)

Function

The function of this module is to insert navigation update state vectors and reschedule the orbital timeline.

Entries

M.NU00 Entered from Timer 2 when scheduled by the DCS Processor module to process a navigation update command.

External

M.CM01 Phase II Control

E.IHBT Inhibit interrupts

E.Q Navigation Update Implementation (M.NU00)

E.QT Phase II Control (M.CM10)

E.ENBL Enable interrupts

Input Data

D.VNUT Navigation update implementation time

D.VUXS }
D.VUYS } Navigation update position vector
D.VUZS }

D.VUDX }
D.VUDY } Navigation update velocity vector
D.VUDZ }

Output Data

V.XDPR }
V.YDPR } Position extra precision words
V.ZDPR }

V.XDSP
V.YDSP } Velocity extra precision words
V.ZDSP }

D.FON Orbit navigation pass flag

V.ONXN
V.ONYN } Previous positions, S-system
V.ONZN }

D.VXS
D.VYS } Positions, S-system
D.VZS }

V.XDN
V.YDN } Previous velocities, S-system
V.ZDN }

D.VXDS
D.VYDS } Velocities, S-system
D.VZDS }

D.VT8S Phase II Control module schedule time for navigation processing

D.VT4S Phase II Control module schedule time for midpoint processing

Status Words

D.VMC7 Mode Code 27

D.FILE Flight Program Status

Telemetry

None.

Initial Conditions

None.

Notes

When a DCS Navigation Update is received and verified, the Navigation Update Implementation module is scheduled for the implementation time and queued-in. It queues itself out before exiting.

The Orbit Navigation module flag is set to cycle the corrector pass.

This module exits to the Phase II Control module, which will return control to Timer 2 rather than returning to this module.

2.42 ORBIT NAVIGATION (NZ)

Function

The function of the Orbit Navigation module is to compute position, velocity, and total acceleration relative to the S-coordinate system during the orbital phases.

Entries

M.NZ00 Entered by the Phase II Control module once every eight seconds during Phase 2.

External

M.GR00 Gravitation Acceleration
M.OA00 Orbit Accelerations
U.SR00 Square Root Utility
U.TR00 Real Time Telemetry Delay Utility

D.VGZ }

V.ONZN } Implementation module

D.VGCZ Guidance Chi Z (Desired yaw gimbal angle) *

D.VTHY Total pitch gimbal angle *
D.VTHZ Total yaw gimbal angle *

V.YDN
V.ZDN

Notes

When running in the Flight Simulation Mode, the guidance chi's are used for the midpoint and endpoint navigation gimbals. In the Flight Mode, the actual gimbals are used.

If a navigation update is received through the Digital Command System, the update will be implemented through the Navigation Update Implementation module and time for the next orbit navigation will be rescheduled.

    NZ100 --> NZ120_L[NZ120 (M. G000) COMPUTE GRAVITATIONAL ACCELERATION]

    NZ130 --> Exit([EXIT NZ500])

    NZ300 --> NZ350[NZ350 SET MID/END FLAG FOR CORR. ENDPOINT PASS]

    NZ130 --> NZ131[NZ131 BO: CAL ACCEL DUE TO GRAVITY AND DRAG]

    NZ350 --> NZ120_R
    NZ400 --> NZ120_R
    NZ120_R --> NZ130
    NZ130 --> NZ131

The flowchart, titled "ORBIT NAVIGATION (NZ)", details the process of updating and correcting orbit navigation data. It begins with "START NZ011" and proceeds to a "NAVIGATION UPDATE PASS". If successful, it moves to a "PREDICTOR NAVIGATION PASS". If not, it calculates midpoint velocity and positions (NZ021), resets the navigation update pass indication (NZ090), and sets a flag for the predicted endpoint pass (NZ100). This leads to computing gravitational acceleration (NZ120) and drag acceleration (NZ130), which then feeds into the "CAL ACCEL DUE TO GRAVITY AND DRAG" step (NZ131) before returning to the predictor pass. If the predictor pass fails, it calculates corrected endpoint velocity and position (NZ201), sets a flag for the corrected endpoint pass (NZ250), and calculates predicted endpoint velocity and position (NZ301). This leads to setting a flag for the corrected endpoint pass (NZ350) and finally the endpoint pass (NZ401), which also feeds into the gravitational acceleration calculation (NZ120). The process concludes with "EXIT NZ500".

2.43 ORBIT ACCELERATIONS (OA)

Function

The function of the Orbit Accelerations module is to calculate the total drag acceleration of the vehicle due to atmospheric conditions.

Entries

M.OA00 Entered by Orbit Navigation during Phase 2.

External

U.FD00 Fixed Point Divide Utility
U.SC00 Sine-Cosine Utility
U.SR00 Square Root Utility

D.VXDSX component of velocity vector, in S-system*
D.VYDSY component of velocity vector, in S-system*
D.VZDSZ component of velocity vector, in S-system*
D.VMTYMidpoint pitch gimbal angle for drag integration*
D.VMTZMidpoint yaw gimbal angle for drag integration*
D.VETYEndpoint pitch gimbal for drag integration
D.VETZEndpoint yaw gimbal for drag integration

D.VYG Y coordinate of position vector, G-system

The components of earth's rotation rate (V.OMX, V.OMY, V.OMZ) about the inertial X, Y, Z Axes must be initialized at mission start.

Notes

The Midpoint/Endpoint flag (D.FON) is set to proper condition by the Orbit Navigation module.

Components of the time varying matrix [MBS] which transforms body coordinates into space-fixed coordinates are stored by rows in X, Y, Z order.

The flowchart is titled "CRBIT ACCELERATIONS (OA)" and is labeled with a page number "2". It consists of several interconnected steps:

  • START OA01: Initiates the process, leading to a decision point "MID-POINT PASS".
  • MID-POINT PASS: If "YES", it proceeds to "CORRECTOR END-POINT NAVIGATION PASS". If "NO", it goes to "OBTAIN END-POINT GIMBAL ANGLES", then "OBTAIN MID-POINT GIMBAL ANGLES", and finally to "OA10: (U, SC00) COMPUTE SIN/COS OF Z GIMBAL ANGLE".
  • START OA16: Initiates the process, leading to "COMPUTE VEHICLE ALTITUDE EQ. 5.4.8", then to "CORRECTOR END-POINT NAVIGATION PASS".
  • CORRECTOR END-POINT NAVIGATION PASS: If "YES", it leads to "(U, TROD) TELEMET ALTIMETER". If "NO", it leads to "(U, TROD) TELEMET ALTIMETER".
  • (U, TROD) TELEMET ALTIMETER: Leads to a decision point "ALTITUDE GREATER THAN HIGH LIMIT".
  • ALTITUDE GREATER THAN HIGH LIMIT: If "YES", it leads to "SET ATMOSPHERIC DENSITY TO ZERO EQ. 5.4.9". If "NO", it leads to "ALTITUDE LESS THAN LOW LIMIT".
  • ALTITUDE LESS THAN LOW LIMIT: If "YES", it leads to "SET ATM. DENSITY TO CONSTANT EQ. 5.4.9". If "NO", it leads to "COMPUTE ATMOSPHERIC DENSITY EQ. 5.4.9".
  • COMPUTE ATMOSPHERIC DENSITY EQ. 5.4.9: Leads to "COMPUTE RELATIVE VELOCITY EQ. 5.4.10", then "COMPUTE THE COS OF THE ANGLE OF ATTACK EQ. 5.4.11", then "COMPUTE THE DRAG COEFF. OF THE VEHICLE EQ. 5.4.12".
  • COMPUTE THE DRAG COEFF. OF THE VEHICLE EQ. 5.4.12: Leads to "DO 5.4.12".
  • DO 5.4.13: Leads to "COMP X DRAG ACCEL COMPONENT EQ. 5.4.13", then "COMP Y DRAG ACCEL COMPONENT EQ. 5.4.13", then "COMP Z DRAG ACCEL COMPONENT EQ. 5.4.13", and finally "EXIT OA25".
  • EXIT OA014: Terminates the process.
  • EXIT OA25: Terminates the process.

2.45 ORBITAL GUIDANCE (OG)

Function

The function of the Orbital Guidance routine is to compute the desired vehicle attitude during periods when no propulsion thrust is available and attitude control is provided by the APS system.

Entries

M.OG00Phase 1 via Non-Interrupt Sequencer once per computation cycle*
(when queued-in). Entered once per second during Phase 2 via*
once per second Timer 2 control module.

External

M.MP00Orbital Guidance Maneuver Processor
U.FD00Fixed Point Divide Utility
U.MM00Matrix Multiply Utility
U.SR00Square Root Utility
M.CC00Chi Computations
M.CC10Chi Telemetry
U.TR00Real Time Telemetry Delay Utility
U.FR00Attitude Freeze Utility
U.AT00Arctangent Utility
U.SC00Sine-Cosine Utility

Input Data

F.SCICFirst pass flag for Spacecraft Control return*
G.MPCKVariable HOP to process or bypass the Maneuver Processor
D.VXSX component of radius vector, in S-system*
D.VYSY component of radius vector, in S-system*
D.VZSZ component of radius vector, in S-system*
D.VXDS X component of velocity vector, in S-system *
D.VYDS Y component of velocity vector, in S-system *
D.VZDS Z component of velocity vector, in S-system *
F.SCAH Flag to indicate S/C returned control
F.MANT Maneuver type flag *
V.RAM Inertial Roll angle in pirads *
V.SPM Inertial Pitch angle in pirads or sine of pitch delta from local horizontal
V.SYW Inertial Yaw angle in pirads or sine of yaw delta from local horizontal
V.CPM Cosine of pitch delta from local horizontal
V.CYW Cosine of yaw delta from local horizontal
D.VGCX Guidance Chi X (Desired roll gimbal angle) *
D.VGCY Guidance Chi Y (Desired pitch gimbal angle) *
D.VGCZ Guidance Chi Z (Desired yaw gimbal angle) *
D.VTHX Total roll gimbal angle *
D.VTHY Total pitch gimbal angle *
D.VTHZ Total yaw gimbal angle *
D.VAP1 Elements of the matrix rotating from S-system to 4-system
thru
D.VAP9
D.FLT Flight Mode indicator
F.SLR Special Local Reference Maneuver first pass flag

Output Data

D.VGCX Guidance Chi X (Desired roll gimbal angle) *
D.VGCY Guidance Chi Y (Desired pitch gimbal angle) *
D.VGCZ Guidance Chi Z (Desired yaw gimbal angle) *
D.VTP1 Cosine Chi Y in 4-system *
D.VTP2 Sine Chi Z in 4-system *
D.VTP3 Sine Chi Y in 4-system *
D.VTP4 Cosine Chi Z in 4-system *
D.VOGR Radius in the Target Plane
V.XSP X component of desired unit thrust vector in S-system *
V.YSP Y component of desired unit thrust vector in S-system *
V.ZSP Z component of desired unit thrust vector in S-system *

Status Words

D.FILE      Flight Program Status
D.VMC7      Mode Code 27

Telemetry

Item PIO Tag Description
V.TLZ4 0434 Z position in target plane
V.TLX4 0444 X position in target plane

Initial Conditions

G.MPCK      Must be set to go to Maneuver Processor

Notes

To initiate special maneuvers, the DCS Processor module modifies the variable HOP constant G.MPCK to initialize for execution of the Special Maneuver.

The flowchart is titled "ORBIT GUIDANCE (OG)" and is labeled with a page number "3" in the top right corner. It consists of several interconnected blocks, each representing a step in the process. The blocks are arranged in a vertical sequence, with some branching paths. The steps are as follows:

  • START (OG0240): The initial step, leading to a decision point.
  • 1ST PASS AFTER S/C CONTROL RETURN: A decision block. If "YES", it leads to a flag-setting step. If "NO", it leads to a nominal maneuver step.
  • NOMINAL MANEUVER AN INERTIAL HOLD: A decision block. If "YES", it leads to setting the MC bit for inertial hold. If "NO", it leads to a local reference maneuver step.
  • SET MC BIT FOR INERT HOLD AFTER S/C CTRL: A processing step that leads to processing attitude freeze.
  • PROCESS ATTITUDE FREEZE (OG0340): A processing step that leads to an exit return.
  • SET S/C LOCAL REF MANEUVER BIT IN MC27: A processing step that leads to executing track local reference maneuver.
  • EXECUTE TRACK LOCAL REF. MANEUVER (OG0680): A processing step that leads to an exit return.
  • SET FLAG FOR NEXT 1ST PASS ON S/C CONTROL: A processing step that leads to a local reference maneuver decision.
  • LOCAL REFERENCE MANEUVER: A decision block. If "YES", it leads to a special local reference maneuver step. If "NO", it leads to a local reference indicator step.
  • SPECIAL LOCAL REFERENCE MANEUVER: A decision block. If "YES", it leads to setting the maneuver type indicator. If "NO", it leads to a local reference indicator step.
  • SET MAN. TYPE INDICATOR FOR INERTIAL HOLD (OG0300): A processing step that leads to a local reference indicator step.
  • LOCAL REFERENCE INDICATOR: A final processing step.

There are also several intermediate steps and labels: OG0480 (COMPUTE UNIT THRUST VECTOR EQ. 5, 5, 9), OG0580 (COMP MANEUVER PARAMETERS FOR S/C), OG0500 (COMPUTE UNIT THRUST VECTOR EQ. 5, 5, 9), OG0640 (SET S/C LOCAL REF MANEUVER BIT IN MC27), OG0660 (EXECUTE TRACK LOCAL REF. MANEUVER), OG0300 (SET MAN. TYPE INDICATOR FOR INERTIAL HOLD), OG0330 (PROCESS ATTITUDE FREEZE), and OG0440 (EXIT RETURN). The flowchart for M-PC01 starts with a 'START' block. It then checks if the PCDF CODE 24 changed during the last second. If 'NO', it proceeds to 'ACCUMULATE DARK PERIOD EMR WORD'. If 'YES', it 'SAVE MODE CODE 24', 'INITIATE INTERRUPTS', 'STORE TIME + ID FOR MC24 IN TABLE 4', 'STORE MC24 IN TABLE 4', and 'ENABLE INTERRUPTS', before returning. The 'ACCUMULATE' block has a loop: if 'NO', it checks 'OR 1/SEC EMR TO 60 SEC EMR WORD'. If 'YES', it proceeds to 'CR 1/SEC EMR TO DARK PERIOD EMR WORD' and then 'RETURN'. If 'NO' to the check, it loops back to 'ACCUMULATE'. If 'YES' to the check, it proceeds to 'CR 1/SEC EMR TO DARK PERIOD EMR WORD' and then 'RETURN'. The 'RETURN' block from 'CR 1/SEC...' loops back to 'ACCUMULATE'. The 'RETURN' block from 'ENABLE INTERRUPTS' loops back to 'CR 1/SEC...'.

  • RETURN (End of routine)

graph TD; M_PC80[START M_PC80] --> V1(( )); V1 --> PC070{HAS POINTER REACHED END OF TABLE}; PC070 -- YES --> INIT[INIT. POINTER = BEGINNING TABLE POINTER]; PC070 -- NO --> PC072{HAS POINTER REACHED END OF SECTOR}; INIT --> PC072; PC072 -- YES --> PC075[ADVANCE POINTER TO NEXT SECTOR]; PC075 --> B7_1[B7]; PC072 -- NO --> PC073[ADVANCE POINTER TO NEXT LOCATION]; PC073 --> PC074[SAVE STORAGE POINTER]; PC074 --> PC075; PC075 --> B7_2[B7]; PC075 --> PC076[END RETURN];

The flowchart is titled "DATA COMPRESSION STORE UTILITY (PC80)". It begins with a "START M_PC80" block. A decision diamond "HAS POINTER REACHED END OF TABLE" (PC070) follows. If "YES", the pointer is initialized to the beginning of the table. If "NO", it proceeds to another decision diamond "HAS POINTER REACHED END OF SECTOR" (PC072). If "YES" at PC072, the pointer is advanced to the next sector (PC075), which also updates register B7. If "NO" at PC072, the pointer is advanced to the next location (PC073). After PC073, the storage pointer is saved (PC074), and the pointer is advanced again (PC075). Finally, the data is stored into the table (PC075), which also updates register B7, and the process ends with a return (PC076).

2.53 SIMULATED PLATFORM GIMBAL ANGLES (PG)

2.55 SIMULATED ACCELEROMETERS (SA)

Function

The function of the Simulated Accelerometers module is to compute simulated velocity increments for a predetermined thrust model during the Flight Simulation Mode of program operation. The method of computation is dependent upon which of the following platform options is in effect:

1. No Platform Inputs Accepted

The Simulated Accelerometers module computes the velocity increments required to simulate platform outputs for the thrust model. These values are used in lieu of actual accelerometer readings throughout the program.

2. Platform Connected and Power Up

The Simulated Accelerometers module computes the simulated velocity increments by adjusting actual accelerometer readings for accelerations due to gravitation and the thrust model.

Entries

M.SA00 Entered from the Non-Interrupt Sequencer once per computation cycle only when operating in the Flight Simulation Mode.

External

U.SC00 Sine-Cosine Utility

Input Data

D.VGCYGuidance Chi Y (Desired pitch gimbal angle)*
D.VGCZGuidance Chi Z (Desired yaw gimbal angle)*
D.VFMC Generated acceleration (Backup)
D.VDTP Intermediate parameter (20*D.VDT) *
D.VTAS Total time elapsed in mission *
D.VDAX Optisyn A change in X velocity *
D.VDBX Optisyn B change in X velocity *
D.VDAY Optisyn A change in Y velocity *
D.VDBY Optisyn B change in Y velocity *
D.VDAZ Optisyn A change in Z velocity *
D.VDBZ Optisyn B change in Z velocity *
D.FMDI Flight mode indicator

Output Data

D.VDAX Optisyn A change in X velocity *
D.VDBX Optisyn B change in X velocity *
D.VDAY Optisyn A change in Y velocity *
D.VDBY Optisyn B change in Y velocity *
D.VDAZ Optisyn A change in Z velocity *
D.VDBZ Optisyn B change in Z velocity *

D.VFY Expected Y platform velocity change
D.VFZ Expected Z platform velocity change

D.VDY Intermediate Y velocity change parameter
D.VDZ Intermediate Z velocity change parameter

The flowchart describes the process of simulating accelerometers. It begins with a start point 'M-SA00'. The first step is to compute the sine and cosine of the command chi Z. This is followed by computing the sine and cosine of the command chi Y. Next, the system computes the expected velocity changes for X, Y, and Z. A decision point follows: if the platform is connected and powered up, the process proceeds to compute the expected velocity changes due to gravity and Earth's rate, then to compute the delta acceleration changes, and finally to exit and return. If the platform is not connected and powered up, the process proceeds to compute the delta acceleration changes directly and then exits and returns.

Upon exit, the sine of the angle will be in accumulator and the cosine of the angle will be in the PQ scaled B0.

2.59 SQUARE ROOT UTILITY (SR)

Function

The Square Root Utility computes the square root of an input argument.

Entries

U.SR00 Entered from any module.

External

None.

Input Data

See Notes.

Output Data

See Notes.

Status Words

None.

Telemetry

None.

Initial Conditions

None.

Notes

Upon entry the input argument must be in the accumulator and the first guess of the square root in the utility temporary location, D.VUTB.

The octal value of the first guess must not be less than one-half of the octal value of the input argument; otherwise, an illegal divide will occur which will cause the square root output to be set to the largest possible value.

*
*
*

Upon exit, the square root of the input argument is in the accumulator.

*

SQUARE ROOT UTILITY (SR)

graph TD; START([START U.SR00]) --> V1(( )); V1 --> SAVE[SAVE RETURN LINKAGE]; SAVE --> V2(( )); V2 --> NEGATIVE{NEGATIVE ARGUMENT}; NEGATIVE -- YES --> RETURN1([RETURN]); NEGATIVE -- NO --> V3(( )); V3 --> ILLEGAL{WILL INPUT VALUES RESULT IN ILLEGAL DIVIDE}; ILLEGAL -- YES --> RETURN1; ILLEGAL -- NO --> V4(( )); V4 --> SR05[SR05]; SR05 --> PERFORM[PERFORM SQUARE ROOT ALGORITHM EQ.13.5.1]; PERFORM --> V5(( )); V5 --> NEGATIVE2{ALGORITHM RESULT NEGATIVE}; NEGATIVE2 -- YES --> RETURN1; NEGATIVE2 -- NO --> V6(( )); V6 --> ITERATIONS{HAVE 3 ITERATIONS BEEN PERFORMED}; ITERATIONS -- YES --> RETURN1; ITERATIONS -- NO --> SR05; SR05 --> RETURN2([RETURN]); ILLEGAL --> SR10[SR10]; SR10 --> OVERFLOW[OVERFLOW PROTECTION SET TO LARGE NUMBER]; OVERFLOW --> RETURN3([RETURN]);

The flowchart, titled "SQUARE ROOT UTILITY (SR)", outlines the following steps:

  • START U.SR00: The initial entry point.
  • SAVE RETURN LINKAGE: A process step that saves the return linkage.
  • NEGATIVE ARGUMENT: A decision diamond. If the answer is YES, the process proceeds to RETURN. If NO, it continues to the next step.
  • WILL INPUT VALUES RESULT IN ILLEGAL DIVIDE: A decision diamond. If the answer is YES, the process proceeds to RETURN. If NO, it continues to the next step.
  • SR05: A process step that performs the square root algorithm (Equation 13.5.1).
  • ALGORITHM RESULT NEGATIVE: A decision diamond. If the answer is YES, the process proceeds to RETURN. If NO, it continues to the next step.
  • HAVE 3 ITERATIONS BEEN PERFORMED: A decision diamond. If the answer is YES, the process proceeds to RETURN. If NO, it loops back to the SR05 step.
  • RETURN: The first return point, reached from the NEGATIVE ARGUMENT, WILL INPUT VALUES RESULT IN ILLEGAL DIVIDE, or ALGORITHM RESULT NEGATIVE steps.
  • SR10: A process step that sets overflow protection to a large number.
  • OVERFLOW PROTECTION SET TO LARGE NUMBER: A process step that follows the SR10 step.
  • RETURN: The final return point, reached from the OVERFLOW PROTECTION SET TO LARGE NUMBER step.

2.60 SWITCH SELECTOR PROCESSOR (SS)

Function

The function of this module is to issue switch selector commands to specified control distributors as a function of time.

Entries

  • M.SS00 Entry to the switch selector check from any module requesting an alternate or special switch selector sequence
  • M.SS05 Entry from Timer 1 to switch selector check routine
  • M.SS10 Entry from the Time Base Set module for proper initialization at each time base change
  • M.SS20 Entry to issue forced reset
  • M.SS30 Entry from Timer 1 to test for a switch selector hung stage
  • M.SS40 Entry from Timer 1 to issue a switch selector stage and address
  • M.SS50 Entry from Timer 1 to verify a switch selector address
  • M.SS55 Entry to check for time to issue the read command after having issued the stage and complemented address
  • M.SS60 Entry from Timer 1 to issue a switch selector read
  • M.SS70 Entry from Timer 1 to reset a switch selector
  • M.SS80 Entry from Timer 1 to issue a switch selector stage and complement address

External

  • M.PC80 Compressed Data Store Utility *
  • E.GP08 Entry to the Timer 1 Halt and Reschedule Executive Routine
  • U.TR00 Real Time Telemetry Delay Utility
  • E.IHBT Inhibit interrupts
  • E.ENBL Enable interrupts
  • E.QT Read Command (M.SS55)
  • E.QT Read Reset (M.SS70)
E.QT Complement Stage and Address (M.SS80)

(-) = Boost *
(+) = Orbit (any bits except sign bit) *

ItemPIO TagDescription
V.SSTL0075Switch Selector Function Indication at Time the Read Command is issued
V.SSFB0500Switch Selector Feedback in error

Initial Conditions

The residual data location reserved for use in conjunction with the Switch Selector EXM instruction must be initialized for flight at mission start. All switch selector time biases will be initialized at mission start as well as all table pointers.

Notes

  1. (1) This module will guarantee all switch selector DOM telemetry.
  2. (2) All switch selector functions and their associated time of issuance are contained in a set of Switch Selector tables referenced by this module for processing.

Switch Selector Nominal and Alternate Event Tables

A. Nominal Event Tables

  1. 1. The events per mission ICD are to be entered in a nominal event table.
  2. 2. The switch selector program is to have the capability to issue events other than the nominal table.

B. Alternate Event Tables

  1. 1. The events are to be entered with delta times referenced to the time the alternate event table is initiated.
  2. 2. All alternate event tables are to be terminated when a new time base is initiated.

C. Event Table Classification (See Table 1)

1. Class 0

  1. a. The nominal event table is considered as class 0.
  2. b. All alternate event tables may be started when the Switch Selector module is operating from the class 0 table.

2. Class 1

  1. a. Class 1 tables will be started immediately upon request.
  2. b. If a switch selector is active, a special entry is made to the forced reset operation and the alternate sequence is started.
  3. c. The interrupted sequence(s) will not be reentered, and upon completion, the Class 1 alternate sequence will assume a class 0 priority level.
  4. d. The nominal S-IVB cutoff switch selector has the highest priority of all switch selector commands.

3. Class 2

  1. a. A class 2 sequence interrupts the current switch selector sequence and must be issued in its entirety.
  2. b. If a switch selector is active, a special entry is made to the forced reset operation and the alternate sequence is started.
  3. c. Upon completion of the class 2 event table control is returned to the table that was in effect when the class 2 table was initiated.
  • d. All events that are late because the class 2 sequence was initiated will be issued at the maximum switch selector rate until normal timing can be resumed.
  • 3. Class 3
    • a. Class 3 events are to be issued at maximum switch selector rate.
    • b. Class 3 tables may be started when the switch selector program is operating from a class 0, or class 4 table.
    • c. Upon completion of the class 3 event table, control is returned to the table that was in effect when the class 3 table was initiated.
    • d. All events that are late because the class 3 sequence was initiated will be issued at the maximum switch selector rate.
  • 4. Class 4
    • a. Class 4 tables are to be concurrent event tables with no restriction on number of events.
    • b. Class 4 tables may be started when the switch selector program is operating from any class table.
    • c. The events of a class 4 table are to be merged with the events of the table that the switch selector is operating from.
    • d. The concurrent table (Class 4) has the lowest priority when the times of the read operation are equivalent.

Switch Selector Table Classes

  • Class 0 Nominal event table
  • Class 1 Alternate event table of highest priority
  • Class 2 Alternate event table of high priority
  • Class 3 Alternate event table of one or two events
  • Class 4 Alternate event table of a finite number of events
    (concurrent table)

The flowchart describes the logic of a Switch Selector Processor (SS). It begins at a START block (SS00). A decision point (NORMAL SWITCH SELECTOR) leads to either a check for requested alternate sequences (SS20) or processing the normal switch selector (SS10). Both paths lead to a decision point (BYPASS THE HUNG STAGE TEST). If YES, it proceeds to execute the hung stage test (SS40); if NO, it also proceeds to SS40. From SS40, the process moves to issue the stage and address (SS50), then verify the address (SS55). A decision point (ADDRESS FEEDBACK GOOD) follows. If NO, it proceeds to issue the read command (SS70); if YES, it also proceeds to SS70. Finally, it issues the reset (SS75) and exits (EXIT RETURN).

A vertical dotted line with a downward-pointing arrow leads to a final block labeled "EXIT SS0060".

The flowchart, titled "SWITCH SELECTOR PROCESSOR (SS)", details the logic for processing switch selector entries. It begins with two parallel paths for "CLASS 4 TABLE ADVANCE ENTRY 1" and "CLASS 4 TABLE ADVANCE ENTRY 2". The first path involves updating time and stage, advancing the switch selector table, and saving time and stage information. The second path involves updating time and stage, saving return hop constants, and resetting the class 4 in progress flag. A central decision point determines if an entry is a "SPECIAL ENTRY" or a "TIME WORD". If a "TIME WORD", it checks if sectors can be changed. If so, it resets the CLA pointer to the beginning of the sector and updates time and stage. If not, it checks if it's the end of a table entry. If yes, it resets the class 4 in progress flag. If no, it processes a non-special entry and updates the SS table pointer. The process concludes with exits to SS2090 or SS2070.

    SetBias --> ExitSS0000[EXIT
SS0000]
    ArePowered -- NO --> AlterExm036[ALTER EXM TO
NOT EXECUTE
PIO 036 (LOAD
SS)]
    AlterExm036 --> SS3040[SS3040
ALTER EXM TO
EXECUTE PIO
036]
    SS3040 --> SS3060[SS3060]
    SS3060 --> BypassHung{BYPASS HUNG
STAGE TEST}
    BypassHung -- YES --> ExitSS4000[EXIT
SS4000]
    BypassHung -- NO --> AreRepeatable{ARE WE IN
REPEATABLE
SIM FLIGHT}
    AreRepeatable -- YES --> ExitSS4000[EXIT
SS4000]
    AreRepeatable -- NO --> ReadRegister[READ SWITCH
SELECTOR
FEEDBACK
REGISTER]
    ReadRegister --> IsHung{IS THERE A
HUNG STAGE}
    IsHung -- YES --> SS3070[SS3070]
    IsHung -- NO --> SS3087[SS3087]
    SS3087 --> ExitSS4000[EXIT
SS4000]
    SS3070 --> IssueReset[ISSUE RESET]
    IssueReset --> SS3090[SS3090]
    SS3090 --> IssueStage[ISSUE STAGE
AND ADDRESS
(M, SS40)]
    IssueStage --> Do[DO]

The flowchart describes the SWITCH SELECTOR PROCESSOR (SS) logic. It begins with a START block (M, SS30) leading to setting the SWITCH SELECTOR HUNG STAGE. This triggers SS3000 (SET SWITCH SELECTOR ACTIVE FLAG), which leads to SS3010 (OBTAIN STAGE AND ADDRESS WORD), then REFORMAT STAGE AND ADDRESS WORD, and finally SAVE STAGE & ADDR. IN TRUE FORM, which feeds into SS3020 (RO). From SS3020, the process branches based on whether the stage is zero. If YES, it proceeds to RESET SWITCH SELECTOR ACTIVE FLAG, then ADVANCE SWITCH SELECTOR TABLE (ENTRY 1), and finally EXIT SS0000. If NO, it proceeds to SS3030 (ARE STAGES POWERED). If YES, it sets bias for address scheduling and exits SS0000. If NO, it alters EXM to not execute PIO 036 (LOAD SS), then SS3040 (ALTER EXM TO EXECUTE PIO 036), then SS3060 (BYPASS HUNG STAGE TEST). If YES, it exits SS4000. If NO, it checks if we are in a repeatable SIM flight. If YES, it exits SS4000. If NO, it reads the SWITCH SELECTOR FEEDBACK REGISTER, then checks if there is a HUNG STAGE. If YES, it proceeds to SS3070 (ISSUE RESET), then SS3090 (ISSUE STAGE AND ADDRESS (M, SS40)), and finally a DO block. If NO, it proceeds to SS3087 and exits SS4000.

M.SS40]) --> V1((V)); V1 --> Stage[STAGE AND
ADDRESS
ISSUANCE]; Stage --> V2((V)); V2 --> SS4000[SS4000]; SS4000 --> Issue[ISSUE SWITCH
SELECTOR
STAGE AND
ADDRESS]; Issue --> V3((V)); V3 --> SS4000_1[SS4000
AO.
18.
SWITCH
SELECTOR TIME
UPDATE]; SS4000_1 --> V4((V)); V4 --> Verify[VERIFY
ADDRESS
(M.SS50)]; Verify --> V5((V)); V5 --> SS4020[SS4020]; SS4020 --> Delay[DELAY FOR DOM.
TELEMETRY]; Delay --> V6((V)); V6 --> Output[OUTPUT S.S.
AND D.O.
REGISTERS VIA
DOM]; Output --> V7((V)); V7 --> Exit([EXIT
SS0060]);

The flowchart illustrates the SWITCH SELECTOR PROCESSOR (SSI) process. It begins with a 'START' block (M.SS40), followed by 'STAGE AND ADDRESS ISSUANCE'. A decision point (V) leads to the 'SS4000' block, which contains 'ISSUE SWITCH SELECTOR STAGE AND ADDRESS'. Another decision point (V) leads to the 'SS4000 AO. 18. SWITCH SELECTOR TIME UPDATE' block. A decision point (V) leads to the 'VERIFY ADDRESS (M.SS50)' block. A decision point (V) leads to the 'SS4020' block, which contains 'DELAY FOR DOM. TELEMETRY'. A decision point (V) leads to the 'OUTPUT S.S. AND D.O. REGISTERS VIA DOM' block. A final decision point (V) leads to the 'EXIT SS0060' block.

graph TD
    Start([START M.SS50]) --> Verify[VERIFY ADDRESS]
    Verify --> Store[STORE COMPLEMENT STAGE AND ADDRESS WORD]
    Store --> Save[SAVE THE COMPUTED FEEDBACK WORD]
    Save --> ArePowered{ARE STAGES POWERED}
    ArePowered -- YES --> UseFeedback[USE COMPUTED FEEDBACK]
    ArePowered -- NO --> ReadSwitch[READ SWITCH SELECTOR FEEDBACK REGISTER]
    ReadSwitch --> IsFeedbackGood{IS FEEDBACK GOOD}
    IsFeedbackGood -- YES --> B2[B2]
    IsFeedbackGood -- NO --> SS5010[SS5010]
    B2 --> SS5500[SS5500]
    SS5010 --> IsFeedbackGood
    SS5500 --> SS5505[SS5505]
    SS5505 --> Start2([START M.SS55])
    Start2 --> ReadTime[READ TIME CHECK]
    ReadTime --> SIVB{S-IVB CUTOFF SWITCH SELECTOR REQUESTED}
    SIVB -- YES --> SetStatus[SET STATUS FLAG TO IND. SIVB CO SS IS SET UP]
    SIVB -- NO --> SS5505
    SetStatus --> SetSSTime[SET SS TIME TO A LARGE VALUE]
    SetSSTime --> ExitReturn1[EXIT RETURN]
    SS5505 --> TimeToIssue{TIME TO ISSUE READ}
    TimeToIssue -- YES --> SS5510[SS5510]
    TimeToIssue -- NO --> SS5510
    SS5510 --> WithinBias{WITHIN BIAS TIME OF READ}
    WithinBias -- YES --> SS5520[SS5520]
    WithinBias -- NO --> SS5530[SS5530]
    SS5520 --> ExitReturn2[EXIT RETURN]
    SS5530 --> ExitMSS60[EXIT M.SS60]
    SS5510 --> SS5590[SS5590]
    SS5590 --> IsFirstFailure{IS THIS FIRST FEEDBACK FAILURE}
    IsFirstFailure -- YES --> SetICR[SET ICR TO SELECT SS CHANNEL B]
    SetICR --> SetFlag[SET FLAG FOR NO CONDITION]
    SetFlag --> MaintainICR[Maintain ICR STATUS WORD SS CHANNEL B]
    MaintainICR --> UTR00[UTR00 TELEMETER FEEDBACK]
    UTR00 --> ExitReturn3[EXIT RETURN]
    IsFirstFailure -- NO --> ExitReturn4[EXIT RETURN]
    SS5590 --> SS5600[SS5600]
    SS5600 --> IssueForcedReset[ISSUE FORCED RESET]
    IssueForcedReset --> DO[DO]

The flowchart describes the SWITCH SELECTOR PROCESSOR (SS) logic. It begins with a START block (M-SS60) leading to SWITCH SELECTOR READ ISSUANCE. This is followed by ISSUE READ COMMAND AND STAGE SELECTED, then SS6000 READ REAL TIME CLOCK, and SS6000 SS7UP0 A0 SWITCH SELECTOR TIME UPDATE. A decision point (IE QT) leads to SCHEDULE RESET READ (M-SS70), which then leads to SS6006 IU TR00) TELEMETER STAGE & ADDR WITH TIME OF READ, and finally a BO (Begin of) block. From BO, the process enters IN TELEM ACQUISITION. If YES, it returns. If NO, it proceeds to COMPRESS SS STAGE AND ADDRESS AND TIME, then S1V8 CUTOFF SWITCH SELECTOR IN PROGRESS. If YES, it goes to SET SAB CD READ COMMAND ISSUED. If NO, it goes to SS6070 OBTAIN STAGE AND ADDRESS WORD, then WAS THIS SS MAN S1V8 ENGINE START ON. If YES, it goes to SET MODE CODE 25 FOR S4B BURN. If NO, it goes to SS6090 OPEN WATER VALVE ISSUED. If YES, it goes to RESET VEC WATER VALVE OPEN REQUEST BIT, then SS6094 SET FLAG TO INDICATE OPEN WATER VALVE, then SS6094 SET FLAG TO INDICATE CLOSED WATER VALVE, and finally RETURN. If NO, it goes to SS6092 CLOSE WATER VALVE SWITCH SELECTOR ISSUED. If YES, it goes to RESET ECS WATER VALVE CLOSE REQUEST BIT, then SS6094 SET FLAG TO INDICATE CLOSED WATER VALVE, and finally RETURN. If NO, it returns directly.

The flowchart illustrates the SWITCH SELECTOR PROCESSOR (SS) algorithm. It begins with a START block (M-SS70), followed by a RESET READ BIT step. This is followed by a RESET RFAD BIT step. Next is the SS7UPD AD SWITCH SELECTOR TIME UPDATE step. This leads to a SCHEDULE HUNG STAGE TEST (M-SS05) step. Then, the ADVANCE SWITCH SELECTOR TABLE step occurs. This is followed by SET RIAS FOR VERIFY ADDRESS SCHEDULING, then SET ON RESET HUNG STAGE BYPASS FLAG. Finally, the process reaches EXIT RETURN, which is linked to SS7030.

The flowchart illustrates the SWITCH SELECTOR PROCESSOR (SS) algorithm. It begins with a START block (M, SS80), followed by a V connector. The next step is COMPLEMENT STAGE AND ADDRESS, which leads to another V connector. This is followed by ISSUE STAGE AND COMPLEMENT ADDRESS, then a V connector. The next step is (SSTUPD) SWITCH SELECTOR TIME UPDATE, followed by a V connector. The next step is (E, QT) SCHEDULE THE READ COMMAND (M, SS55), followed by a V connector. The next step is SS8020 DELAY FOR DOM TELEMETRY, followed by a V connector. The next step is OUTPUT S, S, AND D, D, REGS VIA DOM, followed by a V connector. The final step is SS8030 EXIT RETURN.

The flowchart describes the SWITCH SELECTOR PROCESSOR (SS) logic. It begins at SS0011 (START), followed by a SWITCH SELECTOR TIME UPDATE (SSTUPD). The process then saves the time-to-go to the next stage (SS). A decision is made: if within 500 ms of the next stage, it exits at SS3000. If not, it checks for a TIME UPDATE REQUESTED. If requested, it implements ground bias time and then zeros the time update waiting flag before setting ground bias time and exiting at SS0010. If no time update is requested, it checks if it's an ALTERNATE SEQUENCE REQUESTED. If yes, it exits at SS0170. If no, it computes time for the hung stage test and schedules the hung stage test (M-SS30) before exiting at SS0060.

If the answer is YES, the process proceeds to a block labeled "SS0090 SET SWITCH SELECTOR REQUEST WORD TC ZERO", which then leads to an EXIT block (SS0060). If the answer is NO, the process continues to a block labeled "/GPOB TIMER 1 HALT AND RESCHEDULE". From there, it proceeds to "/SET ALT SEQ IN PROG. IND FOR SIVB CUTOFF", then "/SET CURRENT TABLE IN PROGRESS POINTERS", then "/SET SS REQUEST WORD TO ZERO", and finally to an EXIT RETURN block.

The flowchart describes the SWITCH SELECTOR PROCESSOR (SS) logic. It begins at a START node (SS0111). A decision point (V) leads to a check for 'CLASS 3 ALTERNATE SEQUENCE IN PROGRESS'. If YES, it proceeds to SS0140, which leads to 'RESTORE TABLE IN PROG. PTRS FROM CLASS 2'. If NO, it proceeds to another decision point (V) for 'CLASS 2 ALTERNATE SEQUENCE IN PROGRESS'. If YES, it also proceeds to SS0140. If NO, it proceeds to SS0130, which leads to 'RESTORE TABLE IN PROG. PTRS FROM CLASS 3'. Both restoration paths lead to 'RESTORE ALT. SEQ. IN PROGRESS INDICATOR', which then leads to 'RESTORE TIME IN TR AT START OF ALT. SEQ.'. This step leads to SS0136, which leads to 'RESTORE INCREMENT WORD'. Finally, both paths lead to an EXIT RETURN node.

The main loop involves checking for acquisition gain requests, LOX dump start/stop requests, and LH2 dump stop requests. 2.61 M/F SMOOTHING (ST)

Function

The function of the M/F Smoothing module is to compute and filter the reciprocal value of measured acceleration.

Entries

M.ST00 Entered from the F/M Calculation module.

External

U.FD00 Fixed Point Divide Utility

U.TR00 Real Time Telemetry Delay Utility

Input Data

D.VFOM Total vehicle acceleration determined from accelerometer readings. *

Output Data

D.VMOF Unsmoothed value of M/F *

D.VMFS Filtered value of current M/F

Status Words

None.

Telemetry

ItemPIO TagDescription
D.VMOF2150Unsmoothed value of M/F *
D.VMFS2154Filtered value of current M/F *

Initial Conditions

The current and three previous M/F values (D.VMOF, D.VMF1, ..., D.VMF3), the current and three previous M/F filtered values (D.VMFS, D.VMS1, ..., D.VMS3), and the eight filter coefficients must be initialized at start of mission to appropriate constants for the S-IVB stage.

Notes

This module is called as a subroutine of the F/M Calculations module. To activate this module, the HOP constant D.GMFS is set to go to M.ST00. To bypass this module, D.GMFS is set to go to D.V300.

The output of the M/F filter, D.VMFS, will be limited to a maximum value of .25 \text{ sec}^2/\text{m}. There will also be a rate of change limit per computation cycle of P.MFSR.

This module keeps a three computation cycle history of previous M/F values and filtered M/F values. The following program variables are used to keep these histories:

D.VMF1}History of previous M/F values
D.VMF2
D.VMF3
D.VMS1}History of previous filtered M/F values

D.VMS3

2.62 TIME BASE SET (TB)

Function

This module will perform the following functions upon entry:

  1. 1. Access the Control Program Time Update routine to update the elapsed time in mission and current phase and reset elapsed time in current time base to zero.
  2. 2. Set start time of current time base equal to updated elapsed time in mission.
  3. 3. Access the table advance routines provided by the Switch Selector Processing, Ladder Ramp Processor, and Events Processor modules to position their respective table pointers for the new time bases.

Entries

M.TB00 Entered once by each time base module defined for the mission to initiate the proper time base.

External

M.EP05 Events Processor
M.LR20 Ladder Ramp Processor
M.SS10 Switch Selector Processing
U.TR00 Real Time Telemetry Delay Utility

E.GP09 Control Program Time Update

Input Data

D.VTMR Time in mission at start of reference (RTC scaled B27)
D.VERT Time error associated with last time update

Output Data

D.VTITime from GRR that the current time base was set*
D.FTBCTime base change flag
D.VTBTime elapsed in current time base
D.VTBBTime base biased elapsed time*
D.VTGBAccumulated ground bias time
D.VTBIIndication of Time Base Initiation

Status Words

None.

Telemetry

ItemPIO TagDescription*
D.VTBI0455Indication of Time Base Initiation*

Initial Conditions

The variable HOP (G.LRTB) must be initialized to bypass or access M.LR20, the ladder ramp time base entry during flight or flight simulation, respectively.

Notes

Each entry may be called once and only once by each mission defined time base module to initiate the respective time base.

Interrupt protection must be in effect upon entry to this module. It is the responsibility of the calling module to provide the required interrupt protection during the execution of the Time Base Set module.

TIME BASE SET (TB)

M.TB00

graph TD
    Start([START M.TB00]) --> GPO9([I.E.GPO9] START A NEW TIME REFERENCE)
    GPO9 --> Determine([DETERMINE TIME BASE START TIME])
    Determine --> SetTime([SET TIME IN TIME BASE TO ZERO])
    SetTime --> SetBiased([SET BIASED TIME IN TIME BASE TO ZERO])
    SetBiased --> TROOC([TROOC ZERO ACCUMULATED GROUND BIAS TIME])
    TROOC --> SetFlag([SET TIME BASE CHANGE FLAG])
    SetFlag --> TB000([TB000 (M.SS10) SWITCH SELECTOR TIME BASE ROUTINE])
    TB000 --> TelemInit([I.U.TB00] TELEM. TB INIT INDICATION)
    TelemInit --> TB001([TB001 (M.EP05) EVENT PROC. TB CHANGE ROUTINE])
    TB001 --> FlightSim([FLIGHT SIMULATION RUN IN PROGRESS])
    FlightSim -- YES --> TB004([TB004 (M.LR20) LADDER RAMP ADVANCE])
    FlightSim -- NO --> T.B005([T.B005])
    TB004 --> T.B005
    T.B005 --> Return([RETURN])

The flowchart is titled "TIME BASE SET (TB)". It begins with a start block "START M.TB00". The process then proceeds to "I.E.GPO9 START A NEW TIME REFERENCE", followed by "DETERMINE TIME BASE START TIME", "SET TIME IN TIME BASE TO ZERO", and "SET BIASED TIME IN TIME BASE TO ZERO". A sub-routine "TROOC ZERO ACCUMULATED GROUND BIAS TIME" is called. After setting the time base change flag, the "SWITCH SELECTOR TIME BASE ROUTINE" (TB000) is invoked, which includes "I.U.TB00 TELEM. TB INIT INDICATION" and "I.M.EP05 EVENT PROC. TB CHANGE ROUTINE". A decision point "FLIGHT SIMULATION RUN IN PROGRESS" follows. If "YES", it proceeds to "I.M.LR20 LADDER RAMP ADVANCE" (TB004), which then leads to "T.B005" and finally "RETURN". If "NO", it also leads to "T.B005" and "RETURN".

2.63 TIME BASE 1 (TBL)

Function

This module initiates Time Base 1 when accessed by the Liftoff Search module or when entered on a Timer 2 interrupt scheduled by Events Processor in the repeatable Flight Simulation Mode.

Entries

M.TB15 Entered by the Liftoff Search module when the liftoff discrete is detected, or from Events Processor in repeatable Flight Simulation Mode.

External

M.TB00 Time Base Set

U.D010 Discrete Output Register Set/Reset Utility

E.ENBL Enable interrupts

None.

Notes

The Time Base 1 module alters the Timer 1 HOP constant value, D.GML, to M.ML00 to deactivate the Liftoff Search module and to activate the Minor Loop module when Time Base 1 is initiated.

2.64 TIME BASE 2 (TB2)

*

Function

The Time Base 2 module will initiate Time Base 2 on the occurrence of either the Low Level Sensors Dry "A" (INT2) or the Low Level Sensors Dry "B" (INT6) in Flight Mode, or when entered on a Timer 2 interrupt scheduled by Events Processor in the Repeatable Flight Simulation Mode.

Entries

  • M.TB20 Entered by the Interrupt Processor when the Low Level Sensors Dry "A" Interrupt is detected.
  • M.TB25 Entered from Timer 2 when scheduled by the Events Processor module in Repeatable Sim Flight.
  • M.TB27 Entered by the Interrupt Processor when the Low Level Sensors Dry "B" Interrupt is detected.

External

  • M.TB00 Time Base Set
  • U.TR00 Real Time Telemetry Delay Utility
  • E.ENBL Enable interrupts
  • E.IHBT Inhibit interrupts
  • E.MASK Inhibit INT2 and INT6 processing

Input Data

  • D.VTEX RTC reading at the time the external interrupt was recognized
  • D.VTI Time from GRR that the current time base was set *
  • D.VZDS Z component of velocity vector, in S-system *

Output Data

  • D.KT2 Time Base 2 start time from GRR *

D.VTRS RTC reading to be used by the Control Program Time Update routine
at a new time base start

D.TBID Time Base indicator

D.GTBD Discrete Processor time base HOP constant

D.VTBI Indication of Time Base Initiation

Status Words

D.VMC5 Mode Code 25

D.VMC7 Mode Code 27

Telemetry

ItemPIO TagDescription
D.TBBU0465Time Base 2 Repeatable telemetry
D.VINT0441Interrupt 2 telemetry
D.VINT0441Interrupt 6 telemetry

Initial Conditions

None.

Notes

The downrange velocity reading test module provides a safeguard against starting Time Base 2 on the pad should Time Base 1 be started without liftoff. Furthermore, if Time Base 2 is not established, no subsequent time bases can be started. If guidance reference failure has occurred, this test will be bypassed and Time Base 2 started upon recognition of either INT2 or INT6. *

Once entered, this module will inhibit the Low Level Sense Interrupt for the remainder of the mission.

2.65 TIME BASE 3 (TB3) *

Function

This module will initiate Time Base 3 when either the S-IB Outboard Engines Cutoff "A" (INT 5) or S-IB Outboard Engines Cutoff "B" (DI23) occurs, or if a preset time in Time Base 2 elapses. In the Repeatable Flight Simulation * Mode, it will initiate Time Base 3 on the occurrence of a scheduled Timer 2 interrupt.

Entries

M.TB30 Entered from the Interrupt Processor on occurrence of the S-IB Outboard Engine Out interrupt (INT5).
M.TB35 Entered from Discrete Processor or a Timer 2 in flight mode, or a Timer 2 in Flight Simulation Mode.

External

M.TB00 Time Base Set
E.MASK Inhibit interrupt 5 processing
E.IHBT Inhibit interrupts *
E.ENBL Enable interrupts
U.TR00 Real Time Telemetry Delay Utility

Input Data

D.VTEX RTC reading at the time the external interrupt was recognized
D.VTI Time from GRR that the current time base was set *
F.T3BU Time Backup Entry Flag

Output Data

D.VTRS RTC reading to be used by the Control Program Time Update routine at a new time base start

D.TBID Time base indicator
D.GTBD Discrete Processor time base HOP constant
D.VTBI Indication of Time Base Initiation
D.VDPT Mask word which specifies which time base discretes are to be processed
D.VDPM Mask word which specifies which DI's are to be processed when they change from OFF to ON *
*

Status Words

D.VMC5 Mode Code 25

Telemetry

Item PIO Tag Description
D.VINT 0441 Time Base 3 interrupt telemetry
D.TBBU 0465 Time Base 3 discrete backup telemetry
V.T3TW 0475 Time Base 3 time backup telemetry

Initial Conditions

None.

Notes

This module cannot be executed until the S-IB Propellant Depletion Interrupt (INT5) inhibit is removed. This inhibit will only be removed when the S-IB Outboard Engine Cutoff Enable switch selector function has been issued.

Once entered, this module will inhibit the S-IB Propellant Depletion interrupt for the remainder of the mission.

None.

All entries to this module cannot be executed until the S-IVB Engine Out interrupt (INT4) and S-IVB Engine Out "A" discrete (DI5) inhibits are

removed and the Non-Interrupt Sequencer entry (M.TB47) is queued-in. This will be accomplished at a mission defined time in Time Base 3.

Once this module initiates the appropriate time base, it will inhibit the S-IVB Engine Out interrupt and discrete and queue-out the backup entry M.TB47.

2.67 REAL TIME TELEMETRY DELAY UTILITY (TR)

Function

The function of the Real Time Telemetry Delay Utility module is to guarantee that telemetry items are not output faster than the maximum rate allowed. When the time for telemetry occurs, the module sets the LVDA Mode Register to the required bit configuration and returns to the calling program module which immediately issues the telemetry.

Entries

U.TR00 Entered by any module.

U.TR10 Dummy entry to bypass minor loop error telemetry *
if guidance failure occurs. *

External

None.

Input Data

None.

Output Data

D.VTD Time of last telemetry output

Status Words

None.

Telemetry

None.

Initial Conditions

Time of last telemetry output (D.VTD) must be initialized to zero at start of mission.

Notes

This module should be accessed only through the telemetry macro, TELM, to assure the entry and return requirements of the module are met.

If the TELM macro is not used, the data sector containing the required mode register bit configuration for the item to be telemetered must be in effect on entry to this module. Upon return the next two instructions executed in the calling program module must be CLA and PIO to complete the telemetry operation while interrupt protection is still in effect.

All interrupts are inhibited (MPY instruction) during the test for telemetry output time. When time for telemetry occurs, interrupt protection is extended (DIV instruction) over the total telemetry output operation. This includes the first two instructions executed in the calling module upon return. Interrupts are periodically allowed during the delay loop.

REAL-TIME TELEMETRY DELAY UTILITY (TR)

graph TD; Start([START U.TROO]) --> Inhibit([INHIBIT INTERRUPTS]); Inhibit --> ReadClock([READ REAL TIME CLOCK]); ReadClock --> Decision{SUFFICIENT DELAY FOR TELEMETRY}; Decision -- YES --> SetMode([SET MODE REGISTER]); Decision -- NO --> Delay([DELAY FOR TELEMETRY]); Delay --> B1Out([B1]); SetMode --> UpdateTime([UPDATE TELEMETRY TIME]); UpdateTime --> Exit([EXIT RETURN]);

The flowchart illustrates the logic of the REAL-TIME TELEMETRY DELAY UTILITY (TR). It begins with a 'START U.TROO' block, which leads to 'INHIBIT INTERRUPTS'. This step is influenced by TR10 and B1. Following this, the system 'READ REAL TIME CLOCK'. A decision point then asks if there is 'SUFFICIENT DELAY FOR TELEMETRY'. If 'YES', it proceeds to 'SET MODE REGISTER', then 'UPDATE TELEMETRY TIME', and finally 'EXIT RETURN'. If 'NO', it enters a 'DELAY FOR TELEMETRY' block, which is also influenced by TR20 and TR10, and has a B1 output. The flowchart uses dotted boxes for process blocks and a diamond for the decision point, with arrows indicating the sequence of operations.

2.68 SIMULTANEOUS MEMORY ERROR RECOVERY (TS)

Function

This module will attempt recovery from a Simultaneous Memory Error (TLC) interrupt and provide pertinent data for analysis.

Entries

M.TS00 Entered from the Interrupt Processor on occurrence of the TLC interrupt (INT9).

External

M.PA00 Phase Activator
M.PC80 Data Compression Store Utility
M.SS20 Switch Selector Processing
E.GP07 Timer 2 Halt and Reschedule
E.GP08 Timer 1 Halt and Reschedule

Input Data

G.L2R1Interrupt Processor return HOP constant
D.FPHCPhase change in progress indicator
F.SSACSwitch Selector active flag
D.VDCTTime from GRR (in seconds positioned for data compression)*
D.GTB4HOP constant to Data Compression Table 4
V.BTCComputation cycle count
D.FPHSPhase indicator flag*
G.NSCTNon-Interrupt sequencer control table pointer
D.VTMMElapsed time in mission from GRR to last time update*
D.VMLTExecution time of next Minor Loop*

Output Data

G.L2R1Interrupt Processor return HOP constant
D.VTDTime of last telemetry output*
V.BTCComputation cycle count
D.VMLTExecution time of next Minor Loop*

D.VEMRError Monitor Word
D.VMC5Mode Code 25
D.VICRInternal Control Register
D.VDORDiscrete Output Register
D.FIL1Interrupt Level 1 in progress flag

Telemetry

ItemPIO TagDescription
D.VTEX0441TLC code and RTC
G.L2R10461TLC HOP save

Initial Conditions

None.

Notes

This module resets the Interrupt Processor's HOP constant to return to the beginning of the Non-Interrupt Sequencer table, terminates any switch selector in progress, and halts and reschedules Timer 1 and Timer 2. It returns to the Interrupt Processor unless the TLC occurred during a phase change in which case it exists to the Phase Activator to restart phase initialization.

      MINOR -- NO --> TS080
      TS080 --> SCHEDULE[SCHEDULE NEXT MINOR LOOP]
      SCHEDULE --> TS080

2.69 TIME TILT GUIDANCE (TT)

Function

The function of the Time Tilt Guidance Module is to generate steering commands (guidance chi's) as a function of time from liftoff through the S-IB burn.

Entries

M.TT00 Entered from the Non-Interrupt Sequencer.

External

M.CC10 Chi Computations

U.FD00 Fixed Point Divide Utility

E.Q Chi Computations (M.CC10)

E.Q Time Tilt Guidance (M.TT00)

*

Input Data

D.VTAS Total time elapsed in mission

D.VEOT Time of S-IB engine out

D.KT1 Time Base 1 start time from GRR

D.VXS X component of radius vector, in S-system

D.GTRY Distance from geocentric radius to top of gantry

*

*

*

*

Output Data

D.VGCY Guidance Chi Y (Desired pitch gimbal angle)

D.VGCZ Guidance Chi Z (Desired yaw gimbal angle)

*

*

Status Words

D.VMC5 Mode Code 25

Telemetry

None.

Initial Conditions

D.VTAR, V.TTST, and V.TTF must be initialized to pre-stored values at mission start.

D.VEOT and F.TTA must be initialized to zero at mission start.

Notes

On indication from the Discrete Processor module that engine out has occurred, the Time Tilt Guidance module will freeze guidance chi's for a specified time, and then continue normal time tilt guidance. Variable scaling is incorporated through the use of pseudo-variables. Initialization of the various pitch time tilt segments and yaw time tilt segments for the Time Tilt Guidance module will be executed as a function of time via a time test in the Time Tilt Guidance module.

The flowchart, titled "TIME TILT GUIDANCE (TT)", begins at "START TT51". It proceeds through a series of decision points: "ENGINE OUT OCCURRED IN FIRST SEGMENT" and "ENGINE OUT OCCURRED IN 2ND SEGMENT". If either is "YES", the flow continues to "ENGINE OUT OCCURRED IN 3RD SEGMENT". If "NO" for any of these, the process moves to "STZ DELTA FREEZE TIME TO ZERO EQ.4.4.4", which then leads to "EXIT TT160". If "YES" for the 3rd segment, it proceeds to "TT140 CALC DEL FREEZE TIME FOR 1ST SEG EQ.4.4.4", then "TT150 CALC DEL FREEZE TIME FOR 2ND SEG EQ.4.4.4", and finally "TT160 COMPUTE TOTAL FREEZE TIME EQ.4.4.5". From "TT160 COMPUTE TOTAL FREEZE TIME", the flow moves to "TT165 CALCULATE TILT ARREST TIME EQ.4.4.6", then "ZERO ENGINE OUT TIME", and finally "EXIT TT60".

graph TD; A[START TT320] --> B{LAST YAW SEGMENT}; B -- YES --> C[TT325 SET END OF YAW GUIDANCE FLAG]; B -- NO --> D[GET YAW PARAMETERS FOR NEW SEGMENT]; C --> E[EXIT RETURN]; D --> F[EXIT RETURN];

The flowchart illustrates the TIME TILT GUIDANCE (TT) process. It begins with a start block labeled 'START TT320'. This leads to a decision block 'LAST YAW SEGMENT'. If the answer is 'YES', the process proceeds to a block labeled 'TT325 SET END OF YAW GUIDANCE FLAG', which then leads to an 'EXIT RETURN' block. If the answer is 'NO', the process proceeds to a block labeled 'GET YAW PARAMETERS FOR NEW SEGMENT', which then leads to another 'EXIT RETURN' block.

2.70 PHASE II TIME UPDATE (TU)

Function

This module will access the Control Program Time Update routine and compute the navigation entry time. It will telemeter all time quantities and form the data compression time word.

Entries

M.TU00 Entered at least once per second from the Phase II Control module.

External

E.GP20 Control Program Time Update
U.TR00 Real Time Telemetry Delay Utility

E.ENBL Enable interrupts
E.IHBT Inhibit interrupts

Input Data

D.VTMMElapsed time in mission from GRR to last time update*
D.VTGBAccumulated ground bias time
D.VRTCReal time clock reading at last time update*
D.VERTTime error associated with last time update
D.VTITime from GRR that the current time base was set

Output Data

D.VACTReal Time Clock reading associated with D.VTAS or D.VNTM*
D.VTBTime elapsed in current time base*
D.VTBBTime base biased elapsed time
D.VNTMTime in mission from GRR of navigation extrapolation*
D.VDCTTime from GRR (in seconds positioned for data compression)*

Status Words

None.

Telemetry

ItemPIO TagDescription
D.VTI0561Current time base start time
D.VTB0031Time base elapsed time
D.VTBB0030Time base biased time
D.VNTM0100Time in mission from GRR of navigation extrapolation*
D.VACT0174Real Time Clock reading associated with D.VTAS

Initial Conditions

None.

Notes

The data compression time is set so that the least significant bit is worth 1/2 second and there are ten leading zeros.

M.TU00

graph TD; Start([START M.TU00]) --> Inhibit([E, IHRT) INHIBIT INTERRUPTS]); Inhibit --> ReadClock[READ REAL TIME CLOCK FOR TIME REFERENCE]; ReadClock --> Enable([E, ENRL) ENABLE INTERRUPTS]; Enable --> TelemClock([U, TRO0) TELEMETER REAL TIME CLOCK]); TelemClock --> ComputeNav[COMPUTE NAV EXTRAP. TOTAL TIME IN MISSION]; ComputeNav --> ComputeTimeBase[COMPUTE TIME IN TIME BASE]; ComputeTimeBase --> TelemTimeBase([U, TRO0) TELEMETER TIME IN TIME BASE]; TelemTimeBase --> CalcBiased[CALCULATE TIME IN TIME BASE BIASED]; CalcBiased --> TelemBiased([U, TRO0) TELEMETER TIME IN TIME BASE BIASED]); TelemBiased --> End([EXIT RETURN]); Start2([U, TRO0) TELEMET NAV EXTRAP. TOTAL TIME IN MIS]) --> TelemBaseStart([U, TRO0) TELEMETER TIME BASE START TIME]); TelemBaseStart --> FormData[FORM DATA COMPRESSION TIME WORD]; FormData --> UpdateSystem([E, GP29) SYSTEM TIME UPDATE]; UpdateSystem --> End;

The flowchart illustrates the PHASE II TIME UPDATE (TU) process. It begins with two parallel paths. The left path starts with 'START M.TU00', followed by 'INHIBIT INTERRUPTS', 'READ REAL TIME CLOCK FOR TIME REFERENCE', 'ENABLE INTERRUPTS', 'TELEMETER REAL TIME CLOCK', 'COMPUTE NAV EXTRAP. TOTAL TIME IN MISSION', 'COMPUTE TIME IN TIME BASE', 'TELEMETER TIME IN TIME BASE', 'CALCULATE TIME IN TIME BASE BIASED', and finally 'TELEMETER TIME IN TIME BASE BIASED'. The right path starts with 'U, TRO0) TELEMET NAV EXTRAP. TOTAL TIME IN MIS', followed by 'TELEMETER TIME BASE START TIME', 'FORM DATA COMPRESSION TIME WORD', 'SYSTEM TIME UPDATE', and ends with 'EXIT RETURN'. Both paths converge at the final output step.

2.72 VECTOR CROSS PRODUCT UTILITY (VC)

Function

The function of the Vector Cross Product Utility module is to compute the cross product of two specified vectors.

Entries

U.VC00 Entered by any module.

External

None.

Input Data

See Notes.

Output Data

D.VUTB+1First component of cross product
D.VUTB+2Second component of cross product
D.VUTB+3Third component of cross product

Status Words

None.

Telemetry

None.

Initial Conditions

None.

Notes

Upon entry the accumulator must contain a computer word of the form CLA A;
MPY B where A and B are initial memory locations of the A and B vectors
respectively.

Upon exit:

D.VUTB+1 = A(2) * B(3) - A(3) * B(2)
D.VUTB+2 = A(3) * B(1) - A(1) * B(3)
D.VUTB+3 = A(1) * B(2) - A(2) * B(1)
graph TD; A[START U.VC00] --> B[SAVE RETURN LINKAGE AND INPUT ARGUMENTS]; B --> C[COMPUTE I ELEMENT OF VECTOR EQ.13.8.1]; C --> D[COMPUTE J ELEMENT OF VECTOR EQ.13.8.1]; D --> E[COMPUTE K ELEMENT OF VECTOR EQ.13.8.1]; E --> F[EXIT RETURN];

U.VC00

2.73 VECTOR DOT PRODUCT UTILITY (VD)

Function

The function of the Vector Dot Utility is to compute the dot product of two specified vectors.

Entries

U.VD00 Entered by any module.

U.VD01 Entered by the Matrix Multiply Utility module.

External

None.

Input Data

See Notes.

Output Data

See Notes.

Status Words

None.

Telemetry

None.

Initial Conditions

None.

Notes

Upon entry a computer word is to be in the accumulator with the following format:

(1)      Syllable 1 = CLA P

where P is location of first of the three VEC locations for one vector

(2)      Syllable 0 = MPY Q

where Q is location of first of the three VEC locations for the second vector

Upon exit the dot product P(1) * Q(1) + P(2) * Q(2) + P(3) * Q(3) will be in the accumulator.

VECTOR DOT PRODUCT UTILITY (VD)

U.VD00

U.VD01

graph TD; U00[START U.VD00] --> V00[SAVE RETURN LINKAGE]; U01[START U.VD01] --> V01[SAVE INPUT ARGUMENTS]; V00 --> V01; V01 --> F01[FORM DOT PRODUCT EQ.13.7.1]; F01 --> E01[EXIT RETURN];

The flowchart illustrates the sequence of operations for the VECTOR DOT PRODUCT UTILITY (VD). It begins with two parallel start points: 'START U.VD00' and 'START U.VD01'. From 'START U.VD00', a vertical dotted line leads down to a box labeled 'SAVE RETURN LINKAGE'. From 'START U.VD01', a vertical dotted line leads down to a box labeled 'SAVE INPUT ARGUMENTS'. A horizontal dotted line with an arrowhead pointing right connects 'SAVE RETURN LINKAGE' to 'SAVE INPUT ARGUMENTS'. From 'SAVE INPUT ARGUMENTS', a vertical dotted line leads down to a box labeled 'FORM DOT PRODUCT EQ.13.7.1'. 2.74 WATER VALVE PROCESSOR (WM)

Function

This module will request the issuance of the ECS Water Valve switch selectors to open or to close the water valve.

Entries

M.WM00 Entered initially from Timer 2 at GRR + mission dependent time and subsequently entered at fixed time intervals.

External

E.QTWater Valve Processor (M.WM00)*
U.SSRQSwitch Selector to close ECS Water Valve (M.SS00)
U.SSRQSwitch Selector to open ECS Water Valve (M.SS00)

Input Data

D.FWVFlag which indicates state of water valve (open or close)
D.FLTFlight Mode indicator*

Output Data

None.

Status Words

D.VASW Switch Selector Request Status

Telemetry

None.

Initial Conditions

D.FWV must be initially set to indicate a closed water valve.

Notes

This module is inhibited until GRR + mission dependent time at which time the discretes are read and the next entry into the module is scheduled to occur 300 seconds from now.

If the water valve is already in the desired state, no switch selector is requested.

If a DCS Command has inhibited issuance of the ECS Water Valve switch selectors, no switch selector is requested.

SECTION 4

REQUIREMENTS/MODULE CROSS REFERENCE

4.1 INTRODUCTION

Table 4-1 shows the correspondence between the program requirements in Part I and the flight program module in which the requirement is implemented. The requirements are identified by the Part I paragraph number in which that requirement is established. Some modules (e.g., Phase Initialization) satisfy the requirements listed in several sections of Part I and thus appear more than once in the table.

The information in Table 4-1 provides a means for locating the flight program segment where a particular function is implemented.
